title: Data Streaming
description: Real-time data processing with Kafka, Flink, Spark Streaming, and related technologies

questions.question: What is Apache Kafka?
questions.correctAnswer: High-throughput distributed event streaming platform
questions.explanation: Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform designed for high-throughput, fault-tolerant, low-latency event processing.

questions.question: What is a Kafka topic?
options: Category or feed name to which events are published
questions.correctAnswer: Category or feed name to which events are published
questions.explanation: A Kafka topic is a category or feed name to which events are published by producers.

questions.question: What is a Kafka partition?
options: Ordered, immutable sequence of events within a topic
questions.correctAnswer: Ordered, immutable sequence of events within a topic
questions.explanation: A partition is an ordered, immutable sequence of events within a topic. Each topic is split into partitions for scalability.

questions.question: What is a Kafka broker?
options: Server that stores topic partitions and serves client requests
questions.correctAnswer: Server that stores topic partitions and serves client requests
questions.explanation: A Kafka broker is a server that stores topic partitions and serves client requests.

questions.question: What was ZooKeeper's role in traditional Kafka?
options: Maintain cluster metadata and coordinate brokers
questions.correctAnswer: Maintain cluster metadata and coordinate brokers
questions.explanation: ZooKeeper maintained cluster metadata and coordinated between brokers in traditional Kafka clusters.

questions.question: What is a Kafka producer?
options: Client application that publishes events to topics
questions.correctAnswer: Client application that publishes events to topics
questions.explanation: A Kafka producer is a client application that publishes (writes) events to Kafka topics.

questions.question: What is a Kafka consumer?
options: Client application that subscribes to and reads events
questions.correctAnswer: Client application that subscribes to and reads events
questions.explanation: A Kafka consumer is a client application that subscribes to and reads events from Kafka topics.

questions.question: What is a consumer group?
options: Group of consumers that collectively read from a topic
questions.correctAnswer: Group of consumers that collectively read from a topic
questions.explanation: A consumer group is a group of consumer instances that collectively read from a topic, with each partition read by only one consumer.

questions.question: What are consumer group offsets?
options: Track the reading position in each partition
questions.correctAnswer: Track the reading position in each partition
questions.explanation: Kafka tracks the offset of the last event read by each consumer group for each partition, allowing consumers to resume from where they left off.

questions.question: What is Kafka Connect?
options: Framework for integrating Kafka with external systems
questions.correctAnswer: Framework for integrating Kafka with external systems
questions.explanation: Kafka Connect is a framework for building data pipelines that integrate Kafka with external systems using connectors.

questions.question: What is a source connector in Kafka Connect?
options: Ingests data from external systems into Kafka
questions.correctAnswer: Ingests data from external systems into Kafka
questions.explanation: A source connector imports data from external systems (databases, files, etc.) into Kafka topics.

questions.question: What is a sink connector in Kafka Connect?
options: Exports data from Kafka to external systems
questions.correctAnswer: Exports data from Kafka to external systems
questions.explanation: A sink connector exports data from Kafka topics to external systems (databases, storage, etc.).

questions.question: What is Kafka Streams?
options: Client library for building stream processing applications
questions.correctAnswer: Client library for building stream processing applications
questions.explanation: Kafka Streams is a client library for building stream processing applications and microservices that process data in Kafka topics.

questions.question: What is KSQL?
questions.correctAnswer: Streaming SQL engine for Kafka
questions.explanation: KSQL is a streaming SQL engine that allows you to query, transform, and process data in Kafka using SQL-like syntax.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Kafka Schema Registry?
options: Manage and enforce schemas for Kafka messages
questions.correctAnswer: Manage and enforce schemas for Kafka messages
questions.explanation: Schema Registry manages and enforces schemas for Kafka messages, enabling schema evolution and compatibility checking.

questions.question: What is Avro format in Kafka?
questions.correctAnswer: Binary serialization format with schema
questions.explanation: Avro is a binary serialization format that includes schema information, enabling efficient serialization and deserialization with schema evolution.

questions.question: What is the offset in Kafka?
options: Sequential ID of an event within a partition
questions.correctAnswer: Sequential ID of an event within a partition
questions.explanation: An offset is a sequential ID assigned to each event within a partition, starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 for each new event.

questions.question: What is the leader of a Kafka partition?
options: Broker responsible for all reads and writes to a partition
questions.correctAnswer: Broker responsible for all reads and writes to a partition
questions.explanation: The leader is the broker responsible for all reads and writes to a partition. Followers replicate from the leader.

questions.question: What is a follower in Kafka?
options: Broker that replicates partition data from leader
questions.correctAnswer: Broker that replicates partition data from leader
questions.explanation: A follower is a broker that replicates partition data from the leader to maintain redundancy and fault tolerance.

questions.question: What is ISR in Kafka?
options: In-Sync Replicas - set of brokers that are in sync with leader
questions.correctAnswer: In-Sync Replicas - set of brokers that are in sync with leader
questions.explanation: ISR (In-Sync Replicas) is the set of brokers that are currently in sync with the partition leader and eligible to be elected as leader.

questions.question: What is the replication factor in Kafka?
options: Number of copies of each partition across brokers
questions.correctAnswer: Number of copies of each partition across brokers
questions.explanation: The replication factor determines how many copies of each partition are maintained across different brokers for fault tolerance.

questions.question: What is the minimum.insync.replicas setting?
options: Minimum number of in-sync replicas required for producer writes
questions.correctAnswer: Minimum number of in-sync replicas required for producer writes
questions.explanation: minimum.insync.replicas specifies the minimum number of in-sync replicas required for a producer to successfully write to a partition, ensuring durability.

questions.question: What is unclean.leader.election.enable?
options: Allow leader election from out-of-sync replicas
questions.correctAnswer: Allow leader election from out-of-sync replicas
questions.explanation: When enabled, unclean.leader.election.enable allows a broker that is not in the ISR to be elected as leader, potentially causing data loss.

questions.question: What is acks in Kafka producer?
questions.correctAnswer: Number of broker acknowledgments required
questions.explanation: acks setting in producer determines how many broker acknowledgments are required: 0 (no ack), 1 (leader ack), or all (all in-sync replicas).

questions.question: What is idempotent producer in Kafka?
options: Producer that prevents duplicate sends of same message
questions.correctAnswer: Producer that prevents duplicate sends of same message
questions.explanation: An idempotent producer ensures that each message is delivered exactly once, even if it's retried, preventing duplicates.

questions.question: What is transactional producer in Kafka?
options: Producer that can send messages to multiple partitions atomically
questions.correctAnswer: Producer that can send messages to multiple partitions atomically
questions.explanation: A transactional producer can send messages to multiple partitions and topics atomically, ensuring all messages are committed or none are.

questions.question: What is consumer lag?
options: Difference between latest offset and consumer offset
questions.correctAnswer: Difference between latest offset and consumer offset
questions.explanation: Consumer lag is the difference between the latest offset in a partition and the current offset of the consumer group, indicating how far behind the consumer is.

questions.question: What is the purpose of consumer groups rebalancing?
options: Reassign partitions to consumers when group membership changes
questions.correctAnswer: Reassign partitions to consumers when group membership changes
questions.explanation: Rebalancing reassigns partition ownership among consumers in a group when consumers join, leave, or when partitions are added/removed.

questions.question: What is heartbeat.interval.ms in Kafka consumer?
options: Interval at which consumer sends heartbeats
questions.correctAnswer: Interval at which consumer sends heartbeats
questions.explanation: heartbeat.interval.ms is the interval at which the consumer sends heartbeats to the group coordinator to indicate it's alive.

questions.question: What is session.timeout.ms in Kafka consumer?
options: Maximum time between heartbeats before consumer is considered dead
questions.correctAnswer: Maximum time between heartbeats before consumer is considered dead
questions.explanation: session.timeout.ms is the maximum time between heartbeats before a consumer is considered dead and triggers rebalancing.

questions.question: What is max.poll.records in Kafka consumer?
options: Maximum number of records returned in a single poll
questions.correctAnswer: Maximum number of records returned in a single poll
questions.explanation: max.poll.records limits the maximum number of records returned in a single call to poll(), controlling batch size.

questions.question: What is auto.offset.reset in Kafka consumer?
options: What to do when offset is out of range
questions.correctAnswer: What to do when offset is out of range
questions.explanation: auto.offset.reset determines what to do when there's no initial offset or the offset is out of range: earliest, latest, or none.

questions.question: What is enable.auto.commit in Kafka consumer?
questions.correctAnswer: Whether to automatically commit offsets
questions.explanation: enable.auto.commit controls whether offsets are automatically committed (true) or manually committed by the application (false).

questions.question: What is commitSync in Kafka consumer?
questions.correctAnswer: Synchronously commit offsets
questions.explanation: commitSync() synchronously commits offsets to Kafka, blocking until the commit is acknowledged by the broker.

questions.question: What is commitAsync in Kafka consumer?
questions.correctAnswer: Asynchronously commit offsets
questions.explanation: commitAsync() asynchronously commits offsets to Kafka, returning immediately and allowing the application to continue processing.

questions.question: What is seek in Kafka consumer?
options: Manually set offset for a partition
questions.correctAnswer: Manually set offset for a partition
questions.explanation: seek() allows manually setting the offset for a specific partition, enabling replay or skipping of messages.

questions.question: What is Apache Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Stateful stream processing framework
questions.explanation: Apache Flink is a stateful stream processing framework for distributed, high-performance, exactly-once processing of unbounded data streams.

questions.question: What is a DataStream in Flink?
options: Representation of a stream of data
questions.correctAnswer: Representation of a stream of data
questions.explanation: A DataStream in Flink is a representation of a stream of data that can be transformed using various operations.

questions.question: What is a DataSet in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Representation of a finite dataset
questions.explanation: A DataSet in Flink is a representation of a finite, bounded dataset that can be processed in batch mode.

questions.question: What is a Table in Flink Table API?
options: Relational table abstraction for streams and batches
questions.correctAnswer: Relational table abstraction for streams and batches
questions.explanation: In Flink's Table API, a Table is a relational abstraction that can represent both streaming and batch data, enabling SQL-like operations.

questions.question: What is SQL API in Flink?
options: Query streams and batches using SQL
questions.correctAnswer: Query streams and batches using SQL
questions.explanation: Flink's SQL API allows you to query both streaming and batch data using standard SQL syntax.

questions.question: What is Flink's event time?
questions.correctAnswer: Time when event actually occurred
questions.explanation: Event time in Flink is the time when the event actually occurred (typically embedded in the event data), as opposed to processing time or ingestion time.

questions.question: What is watermark in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Estimate of event time progress
questions.explanation: A watermark in Flink is an estimate of event time progress, used to trigger window computations and handle late data.

questions.question: What is a window in Flink?
options: Finite set of events grouped together
questions.correctAnswer: Finite set of events grouped together
questions.explanation: A window in Flink is a finite set of events grouped together based on time or count, used for aggregations and computations.

questions.question: What is a tumbling window in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed-size, non-overlapping windows
questions.explanation: Tumbling windows are fixed-size, non-overlapping windows where events are assigned to exactly one window.

questions.question: What is a sliding window in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed-size, overlapping windows
questions.explanation: Sliding windows are fixed-size windows that overlap with each other, allowing events to belong to multiple windows.

questions.question: What is a session window in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Windows based on activity gaps
questions.explanation: Session windows group events into sessions based on gaps of inactivity (e.g., user sessions that end after a period of inactivity).

questions.question: What is a global window in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Single window containing all events
questions.explanation: A global window contains all events in the stream, typically used with custom triggers for aggregation.

questions.question: What is a trigger in Flink?
options: Determines when a window is evaluated
questions.correctAnswer: Determines when a window is evaluated
questions.explanation: A trigger in Flink determines when a window is evaluated and results are emitted, based on time or event counts.

questions.question: What is state in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Data maintained during stream processing
questions.explanation: State in Flink is data that is maintained and updated during stream processing, such as counts, aggregations, or user sessions.

questions.question: What is Keyed State in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: State scoped to a key
questions.explanation: Keyed State in Flink is state that is scoped to a specific key, accessible only when processing events with that key.

questions.question: What is Operator State in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: State scoped to an operator
questions.explanation: Operator State in Flink is state that is scoped to a specific operator (e.g., Kafka consumer state), independent of keys.

questions.question: What is a state backend in Flink?
options: Where state is stored and how it's checkpointed
questions.correctAnswer: Where state is stored and how it's checkpointed
questions.explanation: A state backend in Flink determines where state is stored (memory, filesystem, RocksDB) and how it's checkpointed.

questions.question: What is MemoryStateBackend in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Stores state in heap memory
questions.explanation: MemoryStateBackend stores state in Java heap memory, suitable for development and small state workloads.

questions.question: What is RocksDBStateBackend in Flink?
questions.correctAnswer: Stores state in RocksDB (on disk)
questions.explanation: RocksDBStateBackend stores state in RocksDB, an embedded key-value store on disk, suitable for large state that doesn't fit in memory.

questions.question: What is FsStateBackend in Flink?
options: Stores state in memory and checkpoints to filesystem
questions.correctAnswer: Stores state in memory and checkpoints to filesystem
questions.explanation: FsStateBackend stores state in memory and checkpoints to a filesystem (local or distributed), providing a balance between performance and scalability.

questions.question: What is checkpointing in Flink?
options: Periodic snapshots of state for fault tolerance
questions.correctAnswer: Periodic snapshots of state for fault tolerance
questions.explanation: Checkpointing in Flink creates periodic snapshots of state and offsets, enabling fault tolerance and exactly-once processing.

questions.question: What is a savepoint in Flink?
options: Manual checkpoint that can be restored
questions.correctAnswer: Manual checkpoint that can be restored
questions.explanation: A savepoint in Flink is a manual checkpoint that can be restored later, useful for planned upgrades or state changes.

questions.question: What is exactly-once processing in Flink?
options: Each event is processed exactly once, even with failures
questions.correctAnswer: Each event is processed exactly once, even with failures
questions.explanation: Exactly-once processing in Flink ensures that each event is processed exactly once, even in the presence of failures, using checkpointing and transactional sinks.

questions.question: What is Spark Streaming?
questions.correctAnswer: Micro-batch stream processing framework
questions.explanation: Spark Streaming processes live data streams by dividing them into micro-batches, which are processed using Spark's batch processing engine.

questions.question: What is a DStream in Spark Streaming?
questions.correctAnswer: Discretized Stream - sequence of RDDs
questions.explanation: A DStream (Discretized Stream) is a sequence of RDDs representing a stream of data, where each RDD contains data from a specific time interval.

questions.question: What is Structured Streaming in Spark?
options: High-level API for stream processing built on DataFrame API
questions.correctAnswer: High-level API for stream processing built on DataFrame API
questions.explanation: Structured Streaming is a high-level API for stream processing built on the DataFrame API, providing end-to-end fault tolerance and exactly-once semantics.

questions.question: What is a DataFrame in Spark Streaming?
options: Distributed collection of data organized into named columns
questions.correctAnswer: Distributed collection of data organized into named columns
questions.explanation: A DataFrame is a distributed collection of data organized into named columns, used in both batch and streaming processing.

questions.question: What is the batch interval in Spark Streaming?
questions.correctAnswer: Time interval for micro-batch processing
questions.explanation: The batch interval determines how often Spark Streaming creates micro-batches of data for processing (e.g., 1 second, 5 seconds).

questions.question: What is a receiver in Spark Streaming?
options: Component that ingests data from external sources
questions.correctAnswer: Component that ingests data from external sources
questions.explanation: A receiver in Spark Streaming is a component that ingests data from external sources (Kafka, Flume, Kinesis, etc.) into Spark.

questions.question: What is Direct Approach (Kafka Direct Stream) in Spark Streaming?
options: Use receivers to ingest from Kafka
questions.correctAnswer: Query Kafka directly without receivers
questions.explanation: The Direct Approach (Kafka Direct Stream) allows Spark to query Kafka directly without using receivers, improving reliability and parallelism.

questions.question: What is mapWithState in Spark Streaming?
options: Stateful transformation maintaining state across batches
questions.correctAnswer: Stateful transformation maintaining state across batches
questions.explanation: mapWithState is a stateful transformation in Spark Streaming that maintains state across batches, useful for maintaining aggregations or sessions.

questions.question: What is updateStateByKey in Spark Streaming?
options: Stateful aggregation maintaining state across batches
questions.correctAnswer: Stateful aggregation maintaining state across batches
questions.explanation: updateStateByKey is a stateful aggregation in Spark Streaming that maintains and updates state for each key across batches.

questions.question: What is checkpointing in Spark Streaming?
questions.correctAnswer: Save state to fault-tolerant storage
questions.explanation: Checkpointing in Spark Streaming saves state and RDDs to fault-tolerant storage (HDFS, S3) to enable recovery from failures.

questions.question: What is output operations in Spark Streaming?
options: Operations that produce output to external systems
questions.correctAnswer: Operations that produce output to external systems
questions.explanation: Output operations in Spark Streaming produce results to external systems (databases, files, dashboards) like print(), saveAsTextFiles(), foreachRDD().

questions.question: What is foreachRDD in Spark Streaming?
options: Apply function to each RDD in a DStream
questions.correctAnswer: Apply function to each RDD in a DStream
questions.explanation: foreachRDD applies a function to each RDD in a DStream as it's generated, useful for writing data to external systems.

questions.question: What is transform in Spark Streaming?
options: Apply RDD-to-RDD transformation to each batch
questions.correctAnswer: Apply RDD-to-RDD transformation to each batch
questions.explanation: transform applies an arbitrary RDD-to-RDD transformation to each batch in a DStream, providing flexibility for complex operations.

questions.question: What is the difference between Spark Streaming and Flink?
options: Spark uses micro-batches, Flink uses true streaming
questions.correctAnswer: Spark uses micro-batches, Flink uses true streaming
questions.explanation: The key difference is their processing model: Spark Streaming uses micro-batch processing, while Flink uses true streaming with event-by-event processing.

questions.question: What is Kafka Streams vs KSQL?
options: Kafka Streams is Java library, KSQL is SQL interface
questions.correctAnswer: Kafka Streams is Java library, KSQL is SQL interface
questions.explanation: Kafka Streams is a Java library for building stream processing applications, while KSQL is a SQL interface for querying and processing Kafka data using SQL-like syntax.

questions.question: What is Apache Pulsar?
questions.correctAnswer: Multi-tenancy pub-sub messaging system
questions.explanation: Apache Pulsar is a multi-tenancy, high-performance pub-sub messaging system that also supports queueing, streaming, and other patterns.

questions.question: What is the difference between Kafka and Pulsar?
options: Pulsar has multi-tenancy built-in, Kafka added it later
questions.correctAnswer: Pulsar has multi-tenancy built-in, Kafka added it later
questions.explanation: Pulsar was designed with multi-tenancy as a first-class feature from the beginning, while Kafka added multi-tenancy support later through namespaces.

questions.question: What is Apache Beam?
options: Unified programming model for batch and streaming
questions.correctAnswer: Unified programming model for batch and streaming
questions.explanation: Apache Beam is a unified, portable programming model for defining both batch and streaming data processing pipelines.

questions.question: What is a runner in Apache Beam?
options: Execution engine that runs Beam pipelines
questions.correctAnswer: Execution engine that runs Beam pipelines
questions.explanation: A runner in Beam is an execution engine that runs Beam pipelines, such as Spark Runner, Flink Runner, or Google Dataflow Runner.

questions.question: What is windowing in streaming?
options: Grouping events into finite windows for processing
questions.correctAnswer: Grouping events into finite windows for processing
questions.explanation: Windowing in streaming divides the continuous stream of events into finite, processable chunks (windows) based on time or count.

questions.question: What is event time vs processing time?
options: Event time when event occurred, processing time when processed
Event time when processed, processing time when occurred
questions.correctAnswer: Event time when event occurred, processing time when processed
questions.explanation: Event time is when the event actually occurred (embedded in event data), while processing time is when the event is processed by the system.

questions.question: What is late data in streaming?
options: Events that arrive after their event time
questions.correctAnswer: Events that arrive after their event time
questions.explanation: Late data refers to events that arrive at the processing system after their event time has already passed, which can be handled using watermarks and allowed lateness.

questions.question: What is allowed lateness in streaming?
options: Maximum time to wait for late data
questions.correctAnswer: Maximum time to wait for late data
questions.explanation: Allowed lateness is the maximum amount of time a streaming system will wait for late data to arrive before considering it as late and potentially discarding it.
